newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Sierra Leone rebel chief says no peace without him.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel chief says no peace without him.

text.p: Sierra Leonean rebel leader Foday Sankoh said on Thursday he wanted to return home to put on track a peace treaty and denied he was being detained by Nigeria.

"The government in Sierra Leone thinks keeping me out of the peace process will solve the problem but they are mistaken," the leader of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF) told Reuters from the Nigerian capital Abuja.
"My immediate return to my area of control in Sierra Leone will help put the peace process back on track," he said.

RUF forces captured the northern town of Kamakwie, 140 kms (90 miles) from the capital Freetown on Tuesday after heavy fighting that left many bodies on the streets, according to a Sierra Leonean army spokesman.
Sankoh, who has been staying in a luxury hotel in Abuja since March, said his mission was to meet military ruler General Sani Abacha but that had not been possible yet.
"I came here to see President Abacha, the chairman of ECOWAS (Economic Comunity of West African States) for his contribution to the peace accord," he said.
"There is a delay and I have not yet seen him. I think the government in Sierra Leone has a hand in the delay...we can call it psychological warfare," he added.
Nigeria has made no comment on his stay for the past two months.
A newspaper said at the time that he was arrested at Lagos airport when arms were found on him, but he denied this.

"Four pistol bullets were found in the suitcase of my bodyguard," he said, adding he was put up in a government guest house for three weeks before being transferred to Abuja where he had been waiting to see Abacha.
The Nigerian ruler, shunned abroad for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy in the most populous African nation, is nevertheless influential in the West African region.

He has played a key role in ending Liberia's civil war and on Thursday was scheduled to meet Liberian leaders to decide whether to postpone general elections there scheduled for May 30 by ECOWAS leaders.

Abacha, an infantry general who seized power in 1993 in turmoil that followed the annulment of a presidential vote that would have restored democracy in Nigeria, was also meeting Togo's President Gnassingbe Eyadema in Abuja on Thursday.
Sankoh said he was not under any restrictions in Abuja. "I can call anyone and I can go wherever I want," he said.
Witnesses said he is alone except for protocol officials in the $500 a night suite at the top of one of Abuja's leading hotels.
His RUF has fought Sierra Leone troops in a civil war that began in 1991 and has killed at least 10,000.
Nigerian troops played a supporting role to the Sierra Leone army, stationing a battalion of troops in Freetown.

The leadership of the RUF was thrown into confusion in March when one faction outside Sierra Leone said it had deposed Sankoh. But when officials of the group tried to return home, they were held by Sankoh loyalists in Sierra Leone.
